toolu_01TfWJ5YQTouKR5JzrKybAdx.notes:
Method: I read every fold screenshot directly. For the tall -full PNGs I cropped them into 1,500px slices with a small pure-Python PNG decoder, because the full images downscale too far to read. The slices are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/541817b2-200f-49c5-b924-e4e11cf0112a/scratchpad/ux/work/ (e.g. 06-04500.png means launch page y 4,500-6,000), and the script is work/crop.py. Page heights come from the PNG headers; y positions are read from the slices at 1440px width and are approximate (±30px). Nothing in the repo was edited, and no tests or servers were run.

The live API was used read-only: 4 workflows, each with exactly 1 run, all named 'Feature implementation'. results/game/1 and /2 for skeleton-001 return 200 with the failed attempts' checks and error, so earlier attempts can be shown without backend work.

Root cause for the naming problem: workflow/export_state.py:84 returns {"name": "Feature implementation", …}.

Constraints for redesign (testids pinned by tests/project-workflows/*.spec.ts): run-node-list with [data-node-id] children (lanes, guardrails, projects specs); graph-legend with 3 li carrying data-executor (clarity.spec.ts:105-109); node-status-meaning containing 'not workflow completion' (projects.spec.ts:172); node-hint (projects.spec.ts:162,179); projects-info containing 'Read-only' (projects.spec.ts:81); reuse-none/reuse-list and node-events/events-none must be visible (projects.spec.ts:232-256); file-findings-none exact text (clarity.spec.ts:268); tab-assignment/tab-run; run-inputs-facts (7 uses). A compacted design can keep these testids on smaller elements, such as tooltips or collapsed sections, but tests asserting toBeVisible will need updating if content moves behind disclosures.

Truthfulness intent from the earlier slices to preserve in compact form: executor marks (PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY §4.3), 'worker succeeded ≠ workflow complete', and the read-only / CLI-only actions.

Suggested IA direction, one page per question:
- Runs home (all projects): runs newest first, with feature title, status, current or failed step, age, duration and a needs-you flag.
- Run page: a 'Now' banner (step, reason, next command), a timeline with durations, a compact fitted graph, and collapsed run details.
- Node view: full width, sticky step strip with prev/next, sub-tabs with counts (Overview/Checks/Screenshots/Files/Findings/Questions/Task/Events), and an attempt switcher.
- Assignment: routed, per lane, decisions collapsed.

Backend asks, collected:
1. Feature title as definition.name, or a feature_title field.
2. An attention field on RunSummary (waiting questions, awaiting approval, failed node).
3. A copyable next-step command, or the unredacted run path.
4. Per-node attempt result URIs.
5. Controller event fixes: review events for print transport, PID checkpoint as a node-less log, and a reason on candidate failure events.

findings.problem: The run page's first screen (900px) does not say which step is active or failed, why, or what CLI command to run next. The status line is one fixed sentence per status (status.ts:22-30, e.g. 'A graph step or check failed. The workflow did not complete.'), the same for every failed run. Most of the first screen is an 11-fact metadata grid at y≈200-490 (Created, Updated, Last event 'sequence 26', Pinned definition + revision, Feature, Base commit, Source branch, Mode, Deadlines, Permission mode, Finish; RunView.tsx:98-131), then tabs, graph, a 3-line legend and a keyboard hint. Below that sits an empty right panel reading 'Select a node…' (y≈790-1390). Nothing on the page names the failing node, the reason, the review verdict or a next command.
findings.evidence: 04-run-skeleton-001-fold.png / -full.png (1473px): 'Failed · A graph step or check failed', no failing-node callout. Independent review is red in the graph at x≈1130, but the reason 'Blocked by general… 1 P1' appears only on the review node at y≈1113-1280 (08-…-review-fold.png). 13-guardrails-run-fold.png: same generic sentence. The real reason is in results/candidate_ui/2 error.message 'project-workflows-browser: no passing test evidence…; Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown', two clicks and a scroll away. 09-run-fixes-001: 'Succeeded' with no total duration and no integration commit. The only next-step text in the data is event #20 on verify_game ('Continue with python -m workflow automatic <path> --live'), shown at y≈4600 of 07-…-verify-full.png. Event #19 ('not transient… a code fix is a lane repair (RUNBOOK)') is never shown.
findings.user_impact: Every visit to a failed or live run starts with a hunt: click nodes one by one and scroll each to find where it stopped and why. The operator then still has to remember the CLI command, because the viewer never gives one.
findings.data_available: Failing or active node: snapshot.nodes[].status (first failed, running, awaiting_approval or paused node). Reason: the latest status_changed event's message for that node (events.json, e.g. #14 'unit: no passing test evidence…'), plus result.error.message (results/<lane>/<n>, results/candidate_<lane>/<n>) and the review's verdict, reviewers[].status and findings[].severity (reviews/1). Needs backend: a copyable next command, because messages carry a redacted '<path>' (server redactPaths) and the run directory (~/.local/state/agent-workflows/<project>/<feature>/<run>) is not served. A small server field such as summary.next_step {command, reason}, or at least the unredacted run path, would do.
findings.suggestion: Replace the facts grid with a 'Now' banner at the top of the run page. It should show the current or failed step (linked), one line of reason (event message, error.message or review verdict with P0/P1 counts), when it happened and how long ago, and the next CLI command with a copy button. For a succeeded run it shows total duration and the integrated commit. Move the 11 facts into a collapsed 'Run details' disclosure or into the Assignment tab, which already repeats 7 of them.

findings.page: Run page and every node page
findings.problem: No view shows the run's history in time order with durations. Events appear only per node, as the last section at the bottom of each node page (NodeDetail.tsx:466-487). Events whose node_id is null are filtered out everywhere (NodeDetail.tsx:305 keeps only event.node_id === node.node_id), so run-level history such as retries, repairs and controller restarts never appears. Nowhere does the viewer show when each step started or ended, or how long it took.
findings.evidence: skeleton-001.events.json: 26 events. #10,15,18,19,21,22,26 have node_id null, including #19 'worker/game failed identically on attempts 1 and 2; not transient… lane repair (RUNBOOK)' and #21 'Repair 1 applied: checkpoint forked…'. None of them is rendered. Node events sit at y≈19,650 on 06-…-launch-full.png (19,834px page), y≈4,400 on 07-…-verify-full.png and y≈2,525 on 05-…-challenge-full.png. The history (challenge 08:39→08:50 over 3 attempts incl. a KeyboardInterrupt, worker 08:50→09:19, verify 09:19→09:29 with 2 failures and an operator repair, candidate 09:30, review blocked 09:32) must be pieced together from 5 pages.
findings.user_impact: Answers the user's 'when it happened' complaint directly: finding out the order of events, where the time went, or why a verify was retried takes visits to several node pages, each scrolled to the bottom. Some key events cannot be seen at all.
findings.data_available: All client-side: events[].occurred_at/node_id/type/status/attempt/message (including node_id null), inputs.workers[].launch.launch_requested_at and stop.confirmed_at, checks[].started_at/finished_at, review.reviewed_at and reviewers[].launched_at/accepted_at, and challenge.decided_at.
findings.suggestion: Add a run timeline to the run page: one row per step attempt with start, end and duration bars (a compact Gantt or a vertical list), and retries, pauses and repairs as markers. Put run-level (node_id null) events inline, and hide the 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID' log noise behind a 'show controller logs' toggle. Clicking a row opens that node. On node pages, show the node's own start, end and duration next to its status, at the top instead of the bottom.

findings.page: Node pages (…/nodes/<node>), especially launch_<lane>, verify_<lane> and review
findings.problem: Each node page is one long column ordered by pipeline internals, not by what the operator is looking for. On launch_game the page runs: facts, Result (full summary paragraph), 10 open assumptions, then 77 changed files. Each file is ~150px with a 'Findings on this file' h6, 'No review finding names this file.' and a Show source button. Every Markdown file (CLAUDE.md, README.md…) is expanded and fully rendered by default (CreatedFiles.tsx:99, initial view 'rendered' for Markdown). Only then come 'Reported by the worker' (the same summary again), Questions to the operator, Launch receipt, the Task disclosure, Reuse evidence and Events. The page has no section index, anchors, counts or collapsing.
findings.evidence: 06-run-skeleton-001-launch-full.png is 19,834px tall (22 screens). Files run from y≈2,330 to ≈17,240; the P1 finding that failed the run sits inline at y≈4,880 (06-04500 crop). Questions ≈19,320, launch receipt ≈19,390, events ≈19,650. 07-…-verify-full.png is 4,965px: checks begin at y≈2,480, after the same summary and 10 assumptions repeated from launch (ResultFacts, NodeDetail.tsx:157). Screenshots start at ≈3,165 and events at ≈4,400. 08-…-review-full.png: findings table at y≈1,715. On every node the detail heading sits at y≈812, so the first screen shows at most the Kind/Executor/Status row.
findings.user_impact: Finding checks, logs, screenshots, the worker's questions or when a worker started takes 3 to 21 screens of scrolling. The operator has to learn where each item lives on each node type, which is the 'look around to understand what's where' complaint.
findings.data_available: No new data needed: result.changed_files, result.checks, the screenshot entries in result.artifacts, inputs.workers[].questions/launch/stop, and events.
findings.suggestion: Give each node page a compact header (status, when, duration, one-line outcome) and sub-tabs or a sticky in-page index with counts: Overview | Checks (5) | Screenshots (2) | Files (77) | Findings (4) | Questions (0) | Task | Events (7). Render the file list as a dense table (path, findings badge, expand on demand) and start Markdown files collapsed. Put 'Questions to the operator' and a failing check at the top when present. Keep testids such as changed-files, checks-list, screenshots and node-events on the moved sections.

findings.page: Run list, run page, launch_<lane> node
findings.problem: A worker waiting on the operator's answer shows only inside the launch node's 'Questions to the operator' section (WorkerInputs.tsx:262-300). That section renders after the result and every captured file (NodeDetail.tsx:410-414). The run page, the graph node, the run list and the project cards show nothing: the node is 'Running' (per the recent commit 7576a28), and RunSummary has no question field. The only mention of `workflow answer` is inside that buried notice (WorkerInputs.tsx:273).
findings.evidence: 06-…-launch-full.png: 'Questions to the operator' at y≈19,320 of 19,834, below 77 files. 04-run-skeleton-001-fold.png: no question indicator anywhere. contracts/projects/v1.ts:36 runSummarySchema has no question or attention field. inputs: workers[].questions[].answer (null = waiting), workers[].completion.status 'question', completion.question.
findings.user_impact: The user explicitly asks 'is a worker waiting on a question?'. While watching a live run from the Mac, a waiting worker looks exactly like a busy one, and its deadline is paused, so the run can stall unnoticed.
findings.data_available: Run page: inputs.workers[].questions (answer === null, asked_at), completion.status === 'question' and completion.question, all already loaded by RunView (fetchRunInputs). Needs backend for the run list and project level: a per-run attention flag or count on RunSummary (e.g. waiting_questions or needs_operator), so lists need not fetch inputs per run.
findings.suggestion: Show an 'Awaiting your answer' banner at the top of the run page with the question text, when it was asked, and the `workflow answer …` command. Mark the graph node with a distinct badge ('Question'). Add a 'Needs you' badge on the run card and project card once the summary carries it. On the launch node, put the Questions section first when any question is unanswered.

findings.problem: The only way to move between nodes is the graph or a 'Nodes' list at the top of the page. The list repeats the graph as text (RunView.tsx:161 says so: 'The list below is the same graph as text'). Neither is sticky (App.css:345 .run-columns is a plain grid with no position: sticky). The list takes a fixed 1/3 column (grid 1fr/2fr) for the whole page height, so below y≈1,400 the left third of the screen is empty while the detail is squeezed into ~900px. No previous/next-step links exist. On mobile the list pushes the detail down (see the mobile finding).
findings.evidence: 06-…-launch-full.png crops 06-01500 to 06-19500: left column empty from y≈1,400 to 19,834. The node list shows 8 rows × ~70px (y≈840-1,385) with exactly the labels, statuses and attempts of the graph. 08-…-review-01500 crop: the findings table is squeezed into the right 2/3, so the Message and Requirement columns wrap to 20+ lines per finding. After reading the launch node's events at y≈19,650, reaching verify_game means scrolling back ~18,800px.
findings.user_impact: Moving between the worker, its verification and the review (the operator's normal path) costs long scrolls back to the top. Half the screen is wasted, and dense content such as the findings table and check commands is harder to read.
findings.data_available: No new data needed.
findings.suggestion: Drop the duplicate list as a visible column (keep it as a visually hidden or screen-reader equivalent, or fold it into the timeline). Make a compact step strip sticky at the top of node pages (status-coloured chips, current node highlighted, prev/next arrows), and give the detail the full width. tests/project-workflows (lanes.spec.ts:67, guardrails.spec.ts:92/145/311, projects.spec.ts:40) query [data-testid=run-node-list] [data-node-id], so keep that testid on whichever element carries the ordered node links.

findings.page: launch_<lane>, verify_<lane>, candidate, review, Assignment tab
findings.problem: Evidence is filed by pipeline node, and some of it appears two or three times while other items exist in only one deep place. launch_game and verify_game load the same result (both have result_uri …/results/game/3), so its summary (1,470 chars) and 10 open assumptions appear on both pages. On launch_game the summary appears twice more (Result, then 'Reported by the worker', because completion.summary == result.summary; the dedup in WorkerInputs.tsx:314 compares only handoff vs completion). The worker task appears in the Assignment tab and again in the launch node's Task disclosure (NodeDetail.tsx:415). Review findings appear in the review node's table and again inline under files on the launch node. Checks and screenshots appear on verify_<lane> and again per lane on candidate.
findings.evidence: result_uris.txt: launch_game and verify_game → results/game/3. 06-01500 and 07-01500 crops show identical summary and assumption lists. 06-16500/18000 crops: 'Reported by the worker' repeats the summary and assumptions. Where each item lives (desktop, skeleton-001): changed files on launch_game y≈2,330+; checks and logs on verify_game y≈2,480; screenshots on verify_game y≈3,165 and candidate (11-01500 crop, y≈2,200); findings on review y≈1,715; questions on launch_game y≈19,320; task in Assignment y≈2,450 and on launch_game y≈19,550 (collapsed); timing in events at the bottom of each node.
findings.user_impact: The operator has to memorise a different map for each node type. Repeated blocks make long pages longer and make it unclear whether two blocks are the same evidence or different evidence.
findings.data_available: No new data needed: equality can be checked on result_uri and on summary strings.
findings.suggestion: Organise by question, not by node. Show each piece once, where it answers a question: 'What changed' (files + diff) on the worker, 'Did it pass' (checks, logs, screenshots) on verification, 'What reviewers found' on review. Everywhere else, use one-line cross-links such as 'Summary: see worker ›'. When two nodes share a result_uri, show the result facts once. Hide 'Reported by the worker' text that equals result.summary.

findings.page: Project page, workflow page, breadcrumb, run header
findings.problem: Every workflow is named 'Feature implementation', because the exporter hardcodes it (workflow/export_state.py:84). That name is used for the project cards' titles (ProjectsView.tsx:166), the workflow page title 'Feature implementation: runs', the breadcrumb crumb (ProjectsView.tsx:93) and the run header's 'Pinned definition'. What tells workflows apart (the feature slug, and the human feature title in inputs.feature such as 'Pirate Sea Race walking skeleton') is grey secondary text or appears only once the run page loads.
findings.evidence: 02-project-b-fold.png: two identical cards 'Feature implementation', told apart only by grey 'skeleton · 8 nodes · current revision ccdd5a54711d' and 'skeleton-fixes · …'. Live API /api/projects/md-manager/workflows: feature-implementation and workflow-guardrails, both named 'Feature implementation'. Breadcrumb on every run: 'Home / Projects / project-B / Feature implementation / skeleton-001'. inputs.feature is 'Pirate Sea Race walking skeleton' or 'Pirate Sea Race skeleton review fixes'.
findings.user_impact: On the project page and in the breadcrumb the user cannot tell features apart at a glance, and has to open cards to learn which is which.
findings.data_available: workflow_id (feature slug) is in every definition and summary. inputs.feature is per run (one extra request each). Needs backend for list-level titles: export the feature title as definition.name instead of the constant, or add a feature_title field to the definition or RunSummary.
findings.suggestion: Use the feature title (or the slug until the backend supplies it) as the primary label on cards, page titles and breadcrumbs, e.g. 'Walking skeleton (skeleton)'. Demote 'Feature implementation', node counts and revision hashes to secondary text or drop them.

findings.page: Projects list, project page, workflow (runs) page
findings.problem: Reaching a run takes Projects → project → workflow → run, three clicks from /projects. The intermediate levels give no status. Project cards show only name and id (ProjectsView.tsx:130-137). Workflow cards show name, slug, node count and revision. The workflow page lists one run (every workflow has exactly one) with created/updated/revision, and below it a 'Current definition' graph with a legend that takes more space than the list and cannot be clicked. No view shows 'active runs' or 'latest runs' across projects.
findings.evidence: 01-projects-fold.png: two bare cards. 02-project-b-fold.png: two cards, no latest-run status. 03-workflow-skeleton-fold.png: the single run card ('skeleton-001 Failed · updated … · created … · pinned revision …') is followed by a 'Current definition' graph plus legend (y≈320-540). Live API: all 4 workflows have exactly 1 run. Run cards show no duration, failed or current step, feature title, or question flag.
findings.user_impact: To check on a live run the user drills through three near-empty pages, guessing which project and which 'Feature implementation' holds it. Nothing up the hierarchy shows that something needs attention.
findings.data_available: Client-side now: RunSummary.status/updated_at/created_at per workflow via fetchRuns (N requests; 4 workflows today). Needs backend for an efficient version: a project-level or global 'recent runs' endpoint returning RunSummary plus latest run per workflow, ideally with the failed or current node and an attention flag.
findings.suggestion: Make /projects and each project page list runs directly, newest first: feature title, status badge, current or failed step, age ('12 min ago'), duration, and a 'needs you' flag. Pin running and awaiting runs at the top. Fold the workflow level into a filter, or keep it only as the run list. Move 'Current definition' behind a disclosure or drop it, since each run page shows its own pinned graph.

findings.problem: Every time is an absolute UTC ISO timestamp with the full date, from formatTime in status.ts:100-104. Nothing is relative ('4 min ago'), no duration is ever computed, and 'Last event' is shown as a sequence number. Check cards print '2026-09-24 09:28:42 UTC → 2026-09-24 09:28:45 UTC' (NodeDetail.tsx:197) instead of '3 s'. The launch receipt shows launch_requested_at and native_started_at, and the stop time is a separate line at the very bottom ('Stop confirmed at…'), so the worker's working time must be computed by hand (08:50:50 → 09:19:13 = 28 min).
findings.evidence: 04-run-skeleton-001-fold.png: 'CREATED 2026-09-24 08:39:40 UTC · UPDATED 2026-09-24 09:36:07 UTC · LAST EVENT sequence 26'. 07-01500 crop: 5 check cards with start → end timestamps. 06-19500 crop: 'Stop confirmed at 2026-09-24 09:19:13 UTC' at y≈19,780, separate from the Launch receipt at y≈19,390. 03-workflow-skeleton: 'updated 2026-09-24 09:36:07 UTC · created 2026-09-24 08:39:40 UTC'.
findings.user_impact: Doing time arithmetic in your head from a Mac browser in a non-UTC timezone to answer 'how long did this take / is it stuck?'.
findings.data_available: Client-side: summary.created_at/updated_at, events[].occurred_at, checks[].started_at/finished_at, launch.launch_requested_at, stop.confirmed_at, reviewers[].launched_at/accepted_at.
findings.suggestion: Show relative times with the absolute local time in a tooltip, e.g. 'updated 3 min ago'. Show durations everywhere something has a start and an end: run total, step, check ('typecheck · 3 s · exit 0'), worker session. Replace 'Last event: sequence 26' with the last event's message and age. For live runs, show a 'live · refreshed 2 s ago' indicator, since pages poll every 5 s (usePoll.ts:4).

findings.problem: A node shows only its latest result (snapshot result_uri). Earlier failed attempts, with their checks, logs and error, cannot be reached from the viewer, even though the API serves them. What an earlier attempt did survives only as one-line event messages at the bottom of the page. The challenge node says 'earlier attempts are kept in the run directory', which sends the user to the VPS filesystem.
findings.evidence: GET …/skeleton-001/results/game/1 → 200: status failed, error VERIFICATION_BLOCKED 'unit: no passing test evidence or failed tests; integration: …', with 5 checks. results/game/2 → 200. verify_game shows only game/3 (07-…-verify). guardrails candidate events #27-#31 alternate succeeded and failed with the identical message 'Combined revision 1ab6b95…', and the failure reason lives only in results/candidate_ui/2 error. 05-…-challenge-fold: 'ATTEMPTS 3 attempts; this is attempt 3 (earlier attempts are kept in the run directory)'.
findings.user_impact: When a verify was retried or repaired, the operator cannot see what failed the first time or compare attempts, which is exactly the diagnosis they need before a lane repair.
findings.data_available: results/<lane>/<n> for n < current is served (200) today; the viewer could derive URIs from snapshot.nodes[].attempt and the lane. Needs backend for a clean version: an explicit list of attempt result URIs per node (e.g. snapshot.nodes[].attempt_results), plus the challenge's earlier attempts if they should be viewable.

findings.page: All run and node pages, app header
findings.problem: Honesty wording is repeated in long form on every page and pushes content down. Examples: the graph legend (3 full sentences, WorkflowGraph.tsx:29-33), the keyboard hint (RunView.tsx:161), and the status glossary footnote on every run page (RunView.tsx:217). Every node page carries 'Status labels here are historical observations…' (NodeDetail.tsx:488), and a 'Reuse evidence' section that almost always says 'No reuse evidence recorded…' and on non-worker nodes renders before the Result (NodeDetail.tsx:431). Also: 'Findings on this file / No review finding names this file.' ×77 (CreatedFiles.tsx:53,136), 'Ownership:' and gate prose on each verify, a 4-line findings explainer under the review table (ReviewDetail.tsx:324), and an app subtitle about Pi/Claude containment graphs shown on Projects pages (App.tsx:635).
findings.evidence: 04-run-skeleton-001-fold.png: legend + keyboard hint take y≈690-770 (~80px). 12-run-fixes-001-handoff: 'Reuse evidence' comes before 'Result' and says 'No result has been published'. 06-06000 crop: 10 files × 'No review finding names this file.' per screen. 08-01500 crop: 4-line explainer. The app header plus info line take y 0-180 on every page.
findings.user_impact: Roughly 250px of every first screen and thousands of pixels on long pages go to text the daily operator already knows. The content they came for sits further down.
findings.data_available: No new data needed.
findings.suggestion: Keep the truthfulness requirements but make them compact. Give statuses and executors a tooltip or '?' popover. Show one small legend chip row ('solid = agent · dashed = verifier/controller'). Hide empty sections ('no reuse', 'no findings on this file') and show them only when non-empty. Say 'not workflow completion' once in the node status tooltip. Tests pin some of these (graph-legend with 3 li in clarity.spec.ts:105-109, node-status-meaning containing 'not workflow completion' in projects.spec.ts:172, file-findings-none text in clarity.spec.ts:268, reuse-none/events-none in projects.spec.ts:232-256), so update those assertions along with the wording.

findings.problem: At 390px the run facts stack into one column (App.css:420), about 600px tall (y≈330-915). The graph shows 1.5 nodes, the legend takes ~140px, and the node list runs to y≈2,000, so a selected node's detail starts at ≈1,975px. findings.problem: The Run/Assignment tab lives in component state (RunView.tsx:50 useState), so it cannot be linked or bookmarked and resets on reload. The tab sits below the run facts grid, and its own first block repeats 7 of those 11 facts (Assignment.tsx:31-44 vs RunView.tsx:98-131). It then renders the whole decisions.md, then setup, then each worker's full task, then owned paths as a 16-item vertical list, and required checks last. The worker task is also on the launch node.
findings.evidence: 14-run-assignment-full.png is 5,762px. The first screen (14-00000 crop) shows the run facts, then 'Assignment' with Feature, Source branch, Base commit, Mode, Deadlines, Permission mode, Finish again, then decisions.md. The worker task starts at y≈2,450 and required checks at y≈5,400. findings.data_available: No new data needed (inputs.decisions, workers[].task, checks, owned_paths).
findings.suggestion: Put the tab in the route (e.g. …/runs/<run>/assignment, or ?view=assignment in routes.ts). Order the tab per lane: task goal first, required checks and scenarios, then owned paths as a compact inline list. Collapse decisions.md by default with a heading outline. Drop the repeated facts, or move all run facts into this tab.

findings.problem: The breadcrumb stops at the run even though the URL includes /nodes/<node> (ProjectsView.tsx:91-95). The node's name appears only in the info line under the breadcrumb, as a raw id ('Run detail, inspecting node launch_game.', ProjectsView.tsx:104). 'Home' goes to the Pi/Claude skills root, a different product area. The workflow crumb is always 'Feature implementation'. findings.suggestion: Breadcrumb as 'Projects / project-B / Walking skeleton · skeleton-001 / Verify game', with a status dot on the run crumb. Drop the info line on run and node pages, keeping the read-only note once on /projects to satisfy projects.spec.ts:81. Consider making 'Projects' the first crumb instead of 'Home'.

findings.problem: 'Attempt' means four different things, and the numbers disagree. The node list and graph show snapshot attempt ('Design challenge · attempt 3'). Node facts show 'Graph attempt 3'. The launch node shows 'Result attempt 3 (graph node attempt is 1)', because it displays the verify attempt-3 result (NodeDetail.tsx:97). Every challenge event says 'attempt 1' while its message says 'Design challenge attempt 2/3'. The candidate shows 'candidate attempt 1', and the Assignment tab says 'Attempt cap 3 per lane and phase'.
findings.evidence: 05-…-challenge-full.png: node list 'attempt 3' but events #1-#7 all 'attempt 1 — Design challenge attempt 3…'. 06-00000 crop: 'RESULT ATTEMPT 3 (graph node attempt is 1)'. skeleton-001.events.json: challenge events all have attempt 1.
findings.user_impact: Hard to answer 'which try is this and how many tries are left?'. The mismatched numbers look like bugs and lower trust in the page.
findings.data_available: snapshot.nodes[].attempt, result.attempt, events[].attempt, inputs.max_verification_attempts. Needs backend: challenge events should carry the real challenge attempt number.
findings.suggestion: Use one term per concept: 'Try 3 of 3' for verification tries (from max_verification_attempts), 'Run step attempt' only where it differs. Show the attempt switcher (see earlier-attempts-unreachable) instead of parenthetical explanations.

findings.page: review node, launch_<lane> node, run timeline
findings.problem: The event stream is itself incomplete or misleading in places a timeline would expose. skeleton-001's failed review has no events at all (the node says 'No events reference this node'), and reviewers[].launched_at is null. In the guardrails run, 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID …' log entries are recorded as launch_controller status_changed → running after that node succeeded. Candidate failure events carry only 'Combined revision …', with no reason.
findings.evidence: 08-…-review-03000 crop: 'Events for this node · No events reference this node.' skeleton-001.events.json ends at #26 (09:32:32) while the review was accepted at 09:32:31 and the run updated at 09:36:07. reviews_1.json reviewers[].launched_at is null for both. workflow-guardrails-001.events.json #5,8,11,14,17,24,29,32: launch_controller 'running' with a PID message. #28 and #31: candidate failed, 'Combined revision 1ab6b95…'.
findings.user_impact: Any timeline or 'Now' banner built on events would show a worker as running again, or a review with no start time, which confuses 'what is happening right now'.
findings.data_available: Needs backend (controller or exporter): emit review start/verdict events for print transport, record the PID checkpoint as type log with node_id null, and put the failure reason in candidate status events. Client-side workaround: ignore status_changed→running on a node whose latest result succeeded, and use review.reviewed_at as the review end.
findings.suggestion: Fix the controller events. Until then, the viewer's timeline should take the review end from review.reviewed_at and candidate failure reasons from lane result errors, and filter PID checkpoint noise.

data.notes:
Method: I read every fold screenshot directly. For the tall -full PNGs I cropped them into 1,500px slices with a small pure-Python PNG decoder, because the full images downscale too far to read. The slices are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/541817b2-200f-49c5-b924-e4e11cf0112a/scratchpad/ux/work/ (e.g. 06-04500.png means launch page y 4,500-6,000), and the script is work/crop.py. Page heights come from the PNG headers; y positions are read from the slices at 1440px width and are approximate (±30px). Nothing in the repo was edited, and no tests or servers were run.

The live API was used read-only: 4 workflows, each with exactly 1 run, all named 'Feature implementation'. results/game/1 and /2 for skeleton-001 return 200 with the failed attempts' checks and error, so earlier attempts can be shown without backend work.

Root cause for the naming problem: workflow/export_state.py:84 returns {"name": "Feature implementation", …}.

Constraints for redesign (testids pinned by tests/project-workflows/*.spec.ts): run-node-list with [data-node-id] children (lanes, guardrails, projects specs); graph-legend with 3 li carrying data-executor (clarity.spec.ts:105-109); node-status-meaning containing 'not workflow completion' (projects.spec.ts:172); node-hint (projects.spec.ts:162,179); projects-info containing 'Read-only' (projects.spec.ts:81); reuse-none/reuse-list and node-events/events-none must be visible (projects.spec.ts:232-256); file-findings-none exact text (clarity.spec.ts:268); tab-assignment/tab-run; run-inputs-facts (7 uses). A compacted design can keep these testids on smaller elements, such as tooltips or collapsed sections, but tests asserting toBeVisible will need updating if content moves behind disclosures.

Truthfulness intent from the earlier slices to preserve in compact form: executor marks (PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY §4.3), 'worker succeeded ≠ workflow complete', and the read-only / CLI-only actions.

Suggested IA direction, one page per question:
- Runs home (all projects): runs newest first, with feature title, status, current or failed step, age, duration and a needs-you flag.
- Run page: a 'Now' banner (step, reason, next command), a timeline with durations, a compact fitted graph, and collapsed run details.
- Node view: full width, sticky step strip with prev/next, sub-tabs with counts (Overview/Checks/Screenshots/Files/Findings/Questions/Task/Events), and an attempt switcher.
- Assignment: routed, per lane, decisions collapsed.

Backend asks, collected:
1. Feature title as definition.name, or a feature_title field.
2. An attention field on RunSummary (waiting questions, awaiting approval, failed node).
3. A copyable next-step command, or the unredacted run path.
4. Per-node attempt result URIs.
5. Controller event fixes: review events for print transport, PID checkpoint as a node-less log, and a reason on candidate failure events.
